correctness.rationale: The exact Poisson factorial moments imply the displayed influence covariance and O(lambda^2) variance. A product remainder has L1 norm O(lambda), negligible after dividing by sqrt(n)*lambda. Rare-count expansion at 0,1,2 yields tau-2Pois(tau/2); an O(lambda^2) third absolute influence moment gives Lyapunov under n lambda^2->infinity; a no-doubletons argument gives convergence to zero for n lambda^2->0. Subsequence argument proves the iff. The 164-assertion standalone checker cross-verifies explicit formulas and simulations; numerical results are not substituted for proofs.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader fixed-mean covariance and delta-method formulas can supply a small-lambda expansion of individual variances but cannot directly imply Gaussian convergence at a changing mean, its necessary and sufficient threshold, or the finite-intensity centered Poisson joint limit; no triangular uniformity is proved by those theorems. This is a quantitative application of classical occupancy tools, not a claim to invent Poisson convergence.

value.rationale: The finite critical-intensity regime gives 13.9292% rejection for a nominal 5% fixed-parameter normal test. This is a sharp practically motivated calibration boundary for a published Poisson goodness-of-fit test, and the joint rank-one collapse shows that differently weighted marginal normal tests provide the same first-order information when sparse. It is not a gratuitous one-number special case or an unsupported downstream power claim.
